issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode silently changed from EXTERNAL to FIXED — breaking behavior change for existing users
issues.detail: Flipping the default from EXTERNAL to FIXED changes the runtime semantics for every caller who relied on the default. The changelog mentions it under 'fixed' but this is a behavior change, not a bug fix. At minimum the commit message and changelog need to call this out as a breaking default change so the maintainer six months from now isn't chasing why endpointing suddenly behaves differently. State the migration path: callers who want the old behavior must pass TurnDetectionMode.EXTERNAL explicitly.

issues.description: Three things in one patch: new feature (split_sentences), default change (FIXED), and frame-listener fix
issues.detail: This is THREE-PATCHES. Adding split_sentences is an additive feature. Switching the default to FIXED is a behavior change. Switching the VAD-stop listener from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is a bug fix. Each should land separately so each can be reverted independently when something downstream breaks. As submitted, a bisect that lands on this commit tells you nothing.

issues.description: Listener swap from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame may silently drop finalization in non-VAD pipelines
issues.detail: The handler used to react to UserStoppedSpeakingFrame and now reacts only to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame. If an upstream pipeline emits UserStoppedSpeakingFrame without the VAD variant (manual turn signals, push-to-talk, scripted tests), finalize() is never called and transcripts hang until the engine times out. State explicitly that this is intended, or handle both. Right now the diff just renames the type and hopes every caller emits the new one.

issues.description: Gratuitous comment churn: commented-out start_processing_metrics line just gets moved
issues.detail: The `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` line is moved from after the two awaits to before them. If it's dead code, delete it. If it's a TODO, mark it with a TODO and a reason. Moving commented-out code in a diff that's supposed to do something else is noise and makes the diff harder to read for the next person. BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: _enable_vad list-membership check should be a set or tuple, and the variable name is now misleading
issues.detail: `not in [EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED, EndOfUtteranceMode.EXTERNAL]` builds a fresh list every call site that hits this; a tuple is fine and idiomatic. More importantly, `_enable_vad` no longer means 'VAD is on' — it means 'VAD is on AND we're not in one of two pipecat-controlled modes'. Either rename it (`_emit_vad_frames`) or document it inline. As-is, the next maintainer will read `self._enable_vad` and assume the obvious thing.

issues.description: split_sentences config is always overwritten — params.split_sentences=None is coerced to False
issues.detail: `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False)` unconditionally constructs a new SpeechSegmentConfig and overwrites whatever the upstream config builder produced. If the SDK ever ships a non-default SpeechSegmentConfig with more fields, this clobbers it. Either only set the attribute when the user supplied a value, or set just `emit_sentences` on the existing object.

Patch changes default behavior, adds a parameter, and swaps a frame listener. Zero test changes shown. For a service this size that's tolerated in some shops, but the patch should at least say in the commit message how it was validated against a live Speechmatics endpoint. Right now the review has to take 'it works' on faith.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch does real work — adds split_sentences plumbing, fixes the VAD finalization listener, introduces a FIXED turn-detection mode — but it does three things in one commit and silently changes a public default. That is THREE-PATCHES. The frame-listener change from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is the kind of swap that breaks anyone whose pipeline doesn't emit the new variant; either handle both or document the contract. SpeechSegmentConfig is unconditionally overwritten, _enable_vad's name no longer matches what it computes, and a commented-out metrics line got moved instead of decided on. Split the patch, call the default change what it is, and the bug fix should land tomorrow.
